video_prompts.prompt: In a brightly lit studio with a neutral grey background, a three-panel split screen appears. The left panel shows a human hand consciously reaching for and picking up a book. The middle panel displays a semi-transparent human torso, revealing a heart that beats with a steady, rhythmic pulse. The right panel shows a hand near a glowing red stove element. The hand on the right jerks away from the heat source instantly. As each action completes, clear text labels fade in above their respective panels: "Voluntary," "Involuntary," and "Reflex Action." The camera remains in a static, centered medium shot, ensuring all three distinct actions and their labels are clearly visible. The final frame holds on this comparative view.

Within a dark, abstract space representing the nervous system, two animated diagrams materialize. On the left, a simplified brainstem connects to a heart via a glowing blue neural pathway. A slow, rhythmic pulse of light travels from the brainstem to the heart, representing involuntary control. On the right, a cross-section of a spinal cord is shown connected to a hand. A fast, bright pulse of light zips from the hand to the spinal cord and immediately reflects back to the hand's muscles, demonstrating a reflex arc. A fainter signal then continues from the spinal cord up towards the brain. The camera performs a slow zoom-in on the right-side diagram, focusing on the spinal cord. The final frame is a close-up of the reflex arc connection.

On a clean white background, a semi-transparent human silhouette materializes. The central nervous system is highlighted in bright yellow (brain and spinal cord), while the peripheral nerves branch out in light blue. The silhouette is animated to be walking. Its foot makes contact with a sharp, red-glowing tack on the ground. Instantly, a red signal flashes from the foot, up the leg's peripheral nerve to the spinal cord. A yellow motor signal immediately flashes back down, causing the leg to lift rapidly before the red sensory signal even reaches the brain. The camera starts with a full body shot, then quickly zooms to the foot and follows the signal path up the leg. The final frame freezes with the leg lifted, showing the complete reflex arc pathway.

Against a dark, minimalist background, a detailed, medically accurate 3D model of the human brain appears in a uniform grey color. The model has a realistic, slightly glossy texture. It begins a slow 360-degree rotation. As it turns, the large forebrain section is painted with a vibrant blue color. Next, the smaller midbrain section, located centrally, highlights in a bright green. Finally, the brainstem and cerebellum, which form the hindbrain, illuminate in a distinct orange. Simple, clear text labels for "Fore-brain," "Mid-brain," and "Hind-brain" fade in next to their corresponding colored sections. The camera executes a smooth, orbiting shot. The final frame shows the brain in profile, with all three sections clearly colored and labeled.

The scene transitions from the previous shot, pushing in on the colored 3D brain model against a dark background. The focus is the blue-colored forebrain, with its intricate folds and fissures (gyri and sulci) rendered in high detail. The midbrain and hindbrain sections fade to dark, isolating the forebrain. As the camera moves closer, the surface of the cerebrum begins to pulse with a soft, internal white light, suggesting complex neural activity. The text label "Cerebrum" materializes and hovers over the surface. The camera performs a slow, dramatic push-in, gliding over the complex landscape of the cerebral cortex. The final frame is an extreme close-up filling the screen with the cerebrum's folded texture.

The view holds on a close-up of the blue cerebral cortex. Glowing, stylized icons begin to materialize on different areas of its surface to represent its functions. A bright lightbulb icon appears for 'Thinking'. A hand icon forms and clenches into a fist for 'Voluntary actions'. A spinning film reel icon materializes for 'Memory'. Icons for an eye, ear, nose, and hand merge into a single point for 'Sensory integration'. Finally, a stomach icon appears for 'Hunger'. Each icon pulses with white light as its corresponding text label fades in beside it. The camera remains in a static close-up shot. The final frame shows the cerebrum adorned with all five glowing icons and their clear text labels, illustrating its diverse responsibilities.

The full 3D brain model reappears against a dark background, with the midbrain section highlighted in green. To the side, simplified models of a human eye and ear are visible. A flash of light enters the eye model, triggering a glowing yellow signal that travels along a nerve pathway directly to the green midbrain, which pulses in response. Next, a soundwave graphic hits the ear model, sending a separate blue signal along another pathway to the midbrain, causing it to pulse again. The text "Controls Visual & Auditory Reflexes" appears next to the midbrain. The camera starts on the full brain and zooms in slightly to focus on the midbrain and the incoming signal pathways. The final frame shows the midbrain with both signal paths terminating there.

A split-screen view is shown. The left side displays the 3D brain model against a dark background, with the cerebellum highlighted in purple. The right side shows a female gymnast in a brightly lit gymnasium, carefully walking on a balance beam. As the gymnast makes a tiny wobble, the cerebellum on the left flashes with bright neural activity, and her arms adjust to regain balance. She then performs a precise, controlled leap. During the leap's preparation and execution, the cerebellum glows continuously, showing its role in coordination. Text labels for "Posture," "Balance," and "Precision" appear over the glowing cerebellum. The camera is static, holding the split-screen view. The final frame shows the gymnast holding a perfect landing pose while the cerebellum remains brightly lit.

The view is a close-up of the hindbrain's brainstem from the 3D model, set against a dark background. The medulla, at the base of the stem, is highlighted in red, while the pons, located just above it, is highlighted in yellow. The red medulla pulses, and next to it, an animated diagram of blood vessels appears with arrows indicating pressure regulation. The yellow pons pulses, and a diagram of lungs appears beside it, showing a rhythmic inhale-exhale cycle with the label "Respiration Regulation." A diagram of a salivary gland also appears near the medulla. The camera performs a slow tilt upwards, moving from the medulla to the pons. The final frame shows a clear, labeled view of both structures with their function diagrams visible.
